venue.name: Vancouver Island Military Museum
venue.description: The Vancouver Island Military Museum is a volunteer run museum in the heritage Centennial Building on Nanaimo's downtown waterfront, next to Piper Park and a short walk from the Port Theatre and the Nanaimo Museum. It holds more than 25 exhibits covering Canadian military history from the War of 1812 through to Afghanistan, along with the home front, the Merchant Navy and the changing role of women in the armed forces. Admission is $4 for adults, $2 for students and seniors, and free for children under 12. Guided Living History Tours led by veteran volunteers are free and can be tailored for school field trips, community groups and youth organisations.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: A standalone site beside Piper Park with its own accessible, free parking lot. The entrance doors are at the top of the righthand stairs. For ramp access, park in the upper lot and take the ramp to the doors.

venue.nearby_park: Piper Park, immediately beside the museum
venue.hours_notes: 10:00am to 3:00pm Tuesday to Friday, 11:00am to 3:00pm Saturday, and by request. Closed on statutory holidays. Open on Remembrance Day, November 11, 11:15am to 4pm, with free admission for everyone that day.

programs.name: Living History Tour for groups
programs.description: A guided tour led by veteran volunteers, built around the museum's artifacts and themed exhibits and the stories of local people caught up in global events. Tours run from 60 minutes to 2 hours depending on what the group is interested in, and can be tailored from a general overview to a single topic. The tour itself is free. Requests go through a form on the bookable tours page, which asks for a preferred date and time and for the number of people, age range and any accessibility needs. Topics on offer include the First World War, the Second World War, the Cold War and Nanaimo's Diefenbunker, segregation and internment, and peacekeeping. The museum is open Tuesday to Saturday, and also opens by request.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the galleries with a veteran volunteer, stopping at themed displays and looking closely at artifacts, medals and uniforms in the cases. Replica objects and photographs can be brought out to handle during the tour.
programs.our_note: The tour is free but the site never says whether the $4 and $2 admission is charged on top, so ask when you book. Either way it is cheap, and under twelves get in free. No minimum notice is given and the museum only opens Tuesday to Saturday, so give the volunteers plenty of warning.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking on site with ramp access from the upper lot, and Piper Park is right next door. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and bus parking are not mentioned anywhere, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The tour is free. The site does not say whether the $4 adult and $2 student admission is charged as well.

programs.name: Object based learning kit in the classroom
programs.description: Sets of objects such as replica artifacts, medals, uniforms and memorabilia, together with high quality photographs, used as hands on aids during a program. The museum's handout for educators says these can be booked for classroom use or included in a museum tour, and that they come with handouts, activity sheets and lesson plans for the teacher. The same handout invites teachers to propose a program the museum does not already run, including a visit to your classroom. No price, length, group size or notice period is published.
programs.what_children_do: Handle replica artifacts, medals and uniforms and look at archive photographs, working through activity sheets with the objects in front of them.
programs.our_note: This is an offer rather than a scheduled program, so treat it as the opening of a conversation with the education coordinator. Nothing about cost, length or how far ahead to ask is published, and it is a small volunteer run museum, so allow time.
programs.practical_summary: This one comes to your room, so the museum's parking and access do not matter. Cost, length and notice are all unpublished, which makes the first email the important one.

programs.evidence: These can be booked for classroom use or included in a museum tour.

programs.name: Young Explorers interpretive program
programs.description: A booked program for children run by the museum's education and public programs coordinator, with a registration form on the programs page. The one still shown is Decoding the Diefenbunker on 27 August 2026 from 1:00pm to 2:30pm, geared towards ages 7 to 13 with older children welcome and children under 7 needing an adult with them. That date has already passed and the events listing shows no upcoming dates, so the page is out of date. No price is published.
programs.what_children_do: Tour the museum's Cold War exhibit, then sit down to make a cipher for encrypting secret messages, spell their own name in morse code and make a bracelet to take home.
programs.our_note: The only date on the page has already gone by and nothing new is listed, so ask the education coordinator when the next one runs. It is aimed at seven to thirteen year olds, which is older than a daycare group, and the site does not say what it costs.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors at the museum, with free parking and ramp access from the upper lot. No price, no upcoming date, and nothing on the site about washrooms or somewhere to eat.
programs.evidence: This program is geared towards ages 7-13, but older kids are welcome.

images.alt: A low white building with a wide overhanging roof and a small lookout cupola, with outdoor stairs up to the doors, a naval gun on the lawn and a Veterans Wall of Honour sign along the front.
A volunteer in a dark uniform leans over a glass display case and points at something inside while four children crowd in to look.
A gallery wall of Merchant Navy displays with model ships in glass cases, framed photographs, a uniform on a stand and two reading lecterns on the open floor.
A tall exhibit panel headed Pride and Prejudice about Canada's Black Battalion, covered in archive photographs and blocks of text, standing between display cases.

gaps: Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Nowhere for a group to eat a packed lunch is mentioned.
Bus parking is not mentioned. The site says only that the museum has its own accessible free parking lot, with an upper lot for ramp access.
No minimum notice is given for booking a tour. The request form simply asks for a preferred date and time.
No group size limit is published. The form asks how many people are coming, which suggests they size the tour to the group.
How many adults have to come with a school group is not stated.
Whether the $4 adult and $2 student admission is charged on top of the free tour is not stated. This is the single most useful thing to settle on the phone.
The admission prices carry no year or season anywhere on the site.
Whether prices include tax is not stated.

STALE: the programs page still advertises Decoding the Diefenbunker on 27 August 2026, which has passed, and the events listing shows no upcoming events. The home page also still carries a notice about being closed on Thursday August 6th for the volunteer barbecue.

The grade range on the guided tour comes from the curriculum links listed in the educators handout, not from a stated age or grade policy. The museum describes its programming as being for visitors of all ages.
The map on the directions page is a plain address search rather than a marked point, so the location here comes from the street address.
The photographs on the site carry file names in place of alt text, so each image was opened and looked at before its description here was written.
The site gives a second email, oic@militarymuseum.ca, for the general manager. Education and program enquiries go to eppc@militarymuseum.ca.

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different postal codes for the same street address. The street number is the same either way, 100 Cameron Road in downtown Nanaimo, so a satnav will still find it. We use the code that their map and their handout for teachers both give.
